title: Safety symbols and hazard signs
competency: Identify laboratory hazard signs and safety symbols and say what each one means.

keywords.def: Signs posted in a laboratory that warn of dangers such as poison, fire, electricity or germs.
Signs that show what to wear or do to stay safe, such as gloves or hand wash.
Items you wear to protect yourself in the lab, such as goggles, gloves, a lab coat and boots.
Poisonous. It can harm or kill if swallowed, breathed in or touched.
Chemicals that burn skin and eyes or eat away metals.

en.text: A lab can hold dangerous chemicals, living samples, sharp tools and breakable things. Hazard signs are posted to warn of these dangers. For example, toxic means poisonous. Corrosives burn skin and eyes. Flammable materials catch fire easily. Read the sign before you touch anything.

screens.ask: What do you think the sign warns?

screens.title: 1.2.3 Safety symbols and hazard signs
paras: A lab can hold dangerous chemicals and biological specimens. It can also hold sharp instruments and breakable objects.
So lab safety symbols and signs must be posted throughout the workplace.
They warn of possible dangers. They keep lab users safe and informed.

screens.title: Figure 1.6 A) Hazard signs
paras: Each hazard sign warns of one kind of danger.
table: Sign
What it means
What to do (added)
Toxic materials
Poisonous. Can harm or kill if swallowed, breathed in or touched.
Never taste or smell it. Wear gloves. Wash your hands afterwards.
High voltage hazard
Very strong electricity that can badly hurt you.
Keep away. Only trained people work near it.
Corrosives
Chemicals that burn skin and eyes or eat away metals.
Wear goggles and gloves. If it touches you, rinse with plenty of water and tell your teacher.
Flammable materials
Catch fire easily.
Keep them away from flames and heat, such as a Bunsen burner.
Electrical hazard
Danger of electric shock from equipment, wires or sockets.
Keep water and wet hands away. Never touch a damaged plug or wire.
Chemical storage area
The place where chemicals are kept.
Do not go in or take anything without your teacher.
Biological hazard
Living things or samples, such as bacteria, that can spread disease.
Handle only as taught. Wash your hands afterwards.
Health hazard
A substance that can harm your body, for example your lungs, over time.
Use it only as your teacher directs. Do not breathe in fumes.
screens.note: The book shows only the pictures with their names. The meanings and "what to do" advice are added to help you.

screens.title: Which sign warns of burns?
screens.ask: Which sign warns that a chemical can burn your skin?
screens.why: Corrosives burn skin and eyes. The other three are protective symbols.
screens.clue: Look at the hazard signs table: which one is about burns?

screens.title: Match sign and meaning
screens.text: Match each hazard sign to its meaning.
pairs: Poisonous if swallowed, breathed in or touched
Living things that may spread disease
screens.why: Each hazard sign warns of one kind of danger.
screens.clue: Use the "What it means" column of the table.

screens.title: A bottle with a flame
screens.text: Tigist finds a bottle with a flame symbol on its label. A Bunsen burner is lit nearby.
opts: Keep it away from the Bunsen burner and other flames
screens.ans: Keep it away from the Bunsen burner and other flames
screens.why: The flame symbol means flammable materials. They catch fire easily.
screens.clue: What does the flame sign warn about?
screens.worked: Flame sign → flammable materials → they catch fire easily. So keep the bottle away from any flame or heat.

screens.title: Name the danger
screens.ask: Chemicals that burn skin and eyes or eat away metals are called ___.
screens.why: Corrosives burn skin and eyes or eat away metals.
screens.clue: Look at the hazard signs table for burns and metals.

en.text: Hazard signs warn of a danger. Safety symbols show how to protect yourself or where to find help. Gloves protect your hands. Safety glasses protect your eyes. Boots protect your feet. A hand wash sign reminds you to wash. A fire extinguisher sign shows where it is kept.

am.text: የአደጋ ምልክቶች ስለ አደጋ ያስጠነቅቃሉ። የደኅንነት ምልክቶች ራስህን እንዴት እንደምትጠብቅ ያሳያሉ። ጓንት እጅህን ይጠብቃል። የደኅንነት መነጽር ዓይንህን ይጠብቃል። ቦት ጫማ እግርህን ይጠብቃል።

screens.title: On a building site
screens.text: Workers build a new road bridge in Bahir Dar. A blue sign at the gate shows a boot.
screens.ask: What do you think the blue sign tells the workers?
opts: Danger: the ground is on fire
Wear boots to protect your feet here
screens.after: Labs use blue symbols like this too. Read on.

screens.title: Figure 1.6 B) Laboratory safety symbols
paras: Safety symbols show what to wear or do, or where to find help.
table: Symbol
What it means (added)
Gloves
Protect your hands from chemicals, heat and sharp things.
Safety glasses
Protect your eyes from splashes and flying pieces.
Boots
Protect your feet from spills and falling objects.
Face shield
Protects your whole face from splashes.
Hand wash
Wash your hands after lab work.
Fire extinguisher
Shows where the fire extinguisher is. Learn its place before you start.
Protective cloth
A lab coat or other protective clothing covers your skin and clothes.
Hearing protection
Protects your ears from very loud noise.
screens.note: The book shows only the pictures with their names. The meanings are added. Spelling slips in the book's labels ("Saftety glasses", "Hearind protection", "materrials") are corrected here.

screens.title: Symbols that protect
defs: Signs that show what to wear or do to stay safe, or where to find help.
Items you wear to protect yourself: goggles, gloves, a lab coat and boots.

screens.title: Protect or warn?
screens.ask: Which of these is a protective symbol, not a hazard warning?
screens.why: Gloves show what to wear. The others warn of a danger.
screens.clue: Hazard signs warn; safety symbols protect or help.

screens.title: Warn or protect?
screens.text: Does each sign warn of a danger, or protect and help you?
items: It warns of things that catch fire.
It warns of germs and living samples.
It shows where help for a fire is.
They can burn skin and eyes.
It reminds you to clean your hands.
screens.why: Hazard signs warn of a danger. Safety symbols tell you how to stay safe.
screens.clue: Ask: does the sign name a danger, or something you wear or use?

screens.title: Guard your eyes
screens.ask: Safety glasses protect your ___ from splashes.
screens.why: Safety glasses protect your eyes from splashes and flying pieces.

screens.title: Work is finished
screens.text: Kebede has finished his lab work with a bacteria sample. He is about to leave.
screens.ask: Which symbol tells him what to do now?
screens.why: The hand wash symbol reminds you to wash your hands after lab work.
screens.clue: Which symbol is about cleaning after work?
screens.worked: Bacteria can spread disease. After lab work, wash your hands. That is the hand wash symbol.

test.text: Which sign warns that a chemical can burn your skin?
test.why: The corrosives sign is a warning. The others are protective symbols.

test.text: Lab safety signs warn of possible dangers and keep lab users safe and informed.
test.why: That is why signs are posted throughout the lab.
